ScamShield demo

Each link opens a fake scam page served from this computer. Nothing here is a real website.

  1. "Your Chase account is locked"
    A text message link to a copy of Chase's sign-in page.
    Expect: blocked, with the reasons and a button to the real chase.com.
  2. "Pay $1.99 to release your package"
    The most common text-message scam in the US.
    Expect: blocked before any card number is typed.
  3. "Your computer is infected — call Microsoft"
    Fake virus alert that tries to lock the screen. Click anywhere on it.
    Expect: fullscreen undone, tab muted, calm "your computer is fine" screen.
  4. Download AnyDesk (after the fake alert)
    What the fake "Microsoft technician" asks for next.
    Expect: download paused — "Did someone on the phone tell you to install this?"
  5. "Guaranteed 3% daily profit" trading platform
    Fake investment site — the costliest scam type.
    Expect: warning banner; clicking "Connect Wallet" or typing a deposit pauses.
  6. "Verify you are human" (fake CAPTCHA)
    The 2025–26 "ClickFix" trick: click the box, then it says press Win+R, Ctrl+V, Enter.
    Expect: the hidden PowerShell command never reaches your clipboard (paste anywhere to see), and the page is blocked.
  7. "IRS: pay your tax debt with gift cards"
    Government imposter with an arrest threat.
    Expect: blocked — no real agency takes gift cards.
  8. Granny's Quilts (a real-looking small shop)
    Control: an ordinary small business on a new address.
    Expect: nothing at Balanced. On Strict (toolbar → Settings), clicking the card field pauses once.
  9. A site on the public phishing list
    One of ~389,000 known phishing hosts bundled with the extension.
    Expect: replaced by the "known scam" page before it loads.

Also try: right-click any link → Check this link for scams, or paste paypa1.com into the toolbar popup.
